target_customer: AI teams training and serving models on GPU clusters, including neoclouds and AI labs
problem: GPU clusters suffer hardware faults and weak scheduling, and Slurm style tooling is hard to run, so expensive GPUs sit idle or jobs die.
business_model: Source-available software with paid hosted and support offerings; Pluto Hosted priced at $250 per seat per month per company claims
product_category: GPU cluster scheduling and AI infrastructure software

founders.name: Roanak Baviskar
education: UC Santa Cruz, Computer Science and Mathematics

founders.name: Andrew Aikawa
prior_employers: Hive AI (lead machine learning engineer, object detection)
education: UC Berkeley, BA Physics and Computer Science (2017)

technical_complexity.rationale: Fault detection, rescheduling and priority scheduling across large GPU clusters, built on Kubernetes, requires deep infrastructure knowledge.

defensibility.rationale: Source-available code and open scheduler projects are easy to fork or approximate; value depends on reliability know-how and customer relationships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition of Trainy found; a search result says Nvidia acquired Run:ai in 2024, from a competitor page, unverified.

market_need_then: The YC page and tagline frame Slurm as the pain; large model training demand in 2023 created GPU scarcity, but no dated spend data was found.

identity.logo: Trainy Konduktor logo exists on PyPI listings; not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Punchy and opinionated: Goodbye Slurm, Hello Konduktor.

branding.brand_signature: Goodbye Slurm, Hello Konduktor tagline and the conductor themed product name
branding.community_and_virality: Open-source projects Konduktor and Pluto with a Discord and GitHub; Pluto was positioned as a Neptune migration path after Neptune's shutdown announcement.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable tagline and open-source presence, but small footprint and no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Trainy remains a small company selling GPU cluster scheduling and, from 2026, an experiment tracker aimed at Neptune users. Its site claims over 5 million GPU hours managed and logos including DigitalOcean, Paperspace and Linum, all self-reported. Funding appears limited to about 500 thousand dollars from Y Combinator per aggregators, so the story is early and unproven rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: Funding is aggregator only (Caplight, VCBacked, CB Insights, Crunchbase snippet): about $500K from Y Combinator, date unclear (June to October 2023), convertible note per CB Insights; Lightspeed named by one profile, uncorroborated. The company site names Z Venture Capital as a backer without amounts. Not recorded as a round. Competitor search returned 2024 to 2026 material only (Slurm, SkyPilot, Run:ai, Determined), so the list is empty. Konduktor name origin not sourced.
